reference_title: EM 1110-2-2104, Strength Design for Reinforced Concrete Hydraulic Structures (USACE, dated 1 November 2023, published 8 January 2025)

sections.title: Shear strength
sections.summary: Shear strength Vn=Vc+Vs is computed per ACI 318-19 except where this chapter modifies it; EM 1110-2-2400 (outlet works) and EM 1110-2-6053 (performance-based design) provide seismic shear-capacity guidance; deep beams follow ACI 318-19's deep-beam provisions.
sections.body: [p. 35] The shear strength (Vn) provided by concrete (Vc) and reinforcement (Vs) must be computed according to ACI 318-19, except in the cases described in this chapter. Guidance is provided in EM 1110-2-2400 (for outlet works) and EM 1110-2-6053 (for performance-based design) to calculate shear capacity for seismic loads, when applicable. Some RCHS members may meet the definition of a deep beam. These members must be designed according to the deep beam provisions of ACI 318-19.
key_points: The shear strength (Vn) provided by concrete (Vc) and reinforcement (Vs) must be computed according to ACI 318-19, except in the cases described in this chapter (p. 35)
Members meeting the definition of a deep beam must be designed according to the deep beam provisions of ACI 318-19 (p. 35)
sections.applicability: Establishes ACI 318-19 as the shear-design baseline before the RCHS-specific exceptions in this chapter.

sections.title: Shear strength for one-way slabs in reinforced concrete hydraulic structures
sections.summary: For large, flat elements such as walls and foundation slabs (I-, T- and L-walls, U-frames, wells, intake towers, control structures, powerhouse substructures) without shear reinforcement, the nominal shear strength is Vc = [2√(f′c) + Nu/(6 Ag)] bd lbs (Eq 5-1); the ACI 318-19 requirements for members without shear reinforcement are waived. Factored shear must be less than ϕVc unless shear reinforcement is provided; there is no Vc/2 limit as for beams.
sections.body: [p. 35] a. A substantial amount of RCHS is comprised of large, flat elements such as walls and foundation slabs. These elements are found in I-walls, T-walls, and L-walls, U-framed structures, pumping station wells, gate wells, intake towers, hydraulic control structures, and powerhouse substructures. Shear reinforcement is not normally used for these structures. For these elements, the nominal shear strength of the unreinforced concrete sections is determined from equation 5-1. The requirements of ACI 318-19 for shear capacity in members without shear reinforcement are waived for these member types. Vc = [2√(f′c) + Nu/(6 Ag)] bd lbs ([0.17√(f′c) + Nu/(6 Ag)] bd N) (5-1) where: Vc = nominal shear capacity, lbs; f′c = concrete compressive strength, psi (MPa) f′c (the print repeats the symbol); Nu = factored axial load, lbs (N); Ag = gross area of design section, in² (mm²); b = section width, in. (mm); d = distance from extreme compression fiber of driving-side leg to primary wall reinforcement, in. (mm) b. The factored shear in one-way slabs must be less than φVc unless shear reinforcement is provided. There is no requirement to limit the shear capacity to Vc/2 when shear reinforcement is not provided, as is required for beams. Shear reinforcement is not commonly used in walls and slabs. They should normally be designed to eliminate the need for shear reinforcement for constructability and economy.
key_points: The requirements of ACI 318-19 for shear capacity in members without shear reinforcement are waived for these member types (p. 35)
The factored shear in one-way slabs must be less than ϕVc unless shear reinforcement is provided; no limit to Vc/2 as for beams (p. 35)
Walls and slabs should normally be designed to eliminate the need for shear reinforcement (p. 35)

sections.title: Design sections for cantilever walls
sections.summary: Sets the critical shear section location for cantilever walls: at the base of the stem for a construction joint there (with vertical face reinforcement developed into the base for shear friction), or at a distance d from the wall-stem front face (toe) / back face (heel) within the base, per Figures 5-1 (T-type) and 5-2 (L-type); U-frame structures are similar.
sections.body: [p. 35] The critical section for shear depends on the support conditions. When a construction joint is used at the base of a cantilevered stem, the critical section for shear must be [p. 36] taken at the base of the stem. Additionally, vertical reinforcement in both faces of the stem should be developed into the base to ensure shear friction across the joint. The critical section for shear in a base is taken at a distance, d, from the front face of the wall stem for the toe section and at the back face of the wall stem for the heel section. Figure 5-1 and Figure 5-2 shows the critical sections for shear at T-type and L-type walls. U-frame structures are similar. (a) Figure 5-1. Critical sections for shear in cantilever T-type walls [p. 37] (b) Figure 5-2. Critical sections for shear in cantilever L-type walls
key_points: When a construction joint is used at the base of a cantilevered stem, the critical section for shear must be taken at the base of the stem (pp. 35-36)
The critical section for shear in a base is taken at d from the front face of the wall stem for the toe and at the back face of the stem for the heel (p. 36)
figures: Figure 5-1: Critical sections for shear in cantilever T-type walls
Figure 5-2: Critical sections for shear in cantilever L-type walls
sections.applicability: Locating where to check shear in a cantilever retaining/flood wall's stem and base.

sections.title: Shear strength for special straight members
sections.summary: For straight members of box culverts, gate wells or similar structures under uniformly distributed loads with shear, flexure and axial compression (not tension), rectangular, ℓn/d between 1.25 and 9, f′c not more than 6,000 psi, with rigid joints and full-length reinforcement: Vc = [(11.5 − ℓn/d) √(f′c) √(1 + (Nu/Ag)/(5√(f′c)))] bd lbs at 0.15ℓn from the face of the support (Eq 5-2), not greater than 2[12 − (ℓn/d)] √(f′c) bd (Eq 5-3) nor 10√(f′c) bd lbs. U.S. units only.
sections.body: [p. 37] a. The provisions of this paragraph apply only to straight members of box culvert sections, gate wells, or similar structures that satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 5-4b and 5-4c. The stiffening effects of wide supports and haunches are included in determining moments, shears, and member properties. The ultimate shear strength of the member is considered to be the load capacity that causes formation of the first inclined crack. The equations in this section are available only in U.S. (standard) units. b. Members that are subjected to uniformly (or approximately uniformly) distributed loads that result in internal shear, flexure, and axial compression (but not axial tension). c. Members having all of the following properties and construction details: (1) Rectangular cross-sectional shapes. (2) ℓn/d between 1.25 and 9, where ℓn is the clear span in inches. (3) f′c not more than 6,000 psi. (4) Rigid, continuous joints or corner connections. [p. 38] (5) Straight, full-length reinforcement. Flexural reinforcement must not be terminated even though it is no longer a theoretical requirement. (6) Extension of the exterior face reinforcement around corners such that a vertical lap splice occurs in a region of compression stress. (7) Extension of the interior face reinforcement into and through the supports. d. The shear strength provided by the concrete is computed as: Vc = [(11.5 − ℓn/d) √(f′c) √(1 + (Nu/Ag)/(5√(f′c)))] bd lbs (5-2) at a distance of 0.15 ℓn from the face of the support. e. The shear strength provided by the concrete is not to be taken greater than Vc = 2[12 − (ℓn/d)] √(f′c) bd lbs (5-3) and not exceed 10√(f′c) bd lbs.
key_points: Applies only to straight members of box culvert sections, gate wells, or similar structures satisfying paragraphs 5-4b and 5-4c; U.S. (standard) units only (p. 37)
ℓn/d between 1.25 and 9 (ℓn clear span in inches); f′c not more than 6,000 psi; no axial tension (p. 37)
Vc = [(11.5 − ℓn/d) √(f′c) √(1 + (Nu/Ag)/(5√(f′c)))] bd lbs (Eq 5-2) at a distance of 0.15ℓn from the face of the support (p. 38)
Vc is not to be taken greater than 2[12 − (ℓn/d)] √(f′c) bd lbs (Eq 5-3) and not exceed 10√(f′c) bd lbs (p. 38)

sections.title: Shear strength for curved members
sections.summary: For uniformly loaded, curved, cast-in-place members with R/d>2.25 (R=radius of curvature to the member centerline), Eq 5-4 gives Vc at points of maximum shear, capped at 10*sqrt(fc')*b*d; US units only.
sections.body: [p. 38] At points of maximum shear, for uniformly loaded, curved, cast-in-place members with R/d > 2.25, where R is the radius curvature to the centerline of the member, the shear strength provided by the concrete is computed as shown below. This equation is available only in U.S. (standard) English units. Vc = [4√(f′c) √(1 + (Nu/Ag)/(4√(f′c)))] bd lbs (5-4) and not exceed: 10√(f′c) bd lbs.
key_points: Uniformly loaded, curved, cast-in-place members with R/d > 2.25 (R radius of curvature to the centerline): Vc = [4√(f′c) √(1 + (Nu/Ag)/(4√(f′c)))] bd lbs (Eq 5-4), not exceeding 10√(f′c) bd lbs (p. 38)

sections.title: Mandatory requirements
sections.summary: Restates that Vc must follow ACI 318-19 except as modified in this chapter, and that cantilever-wall, special-straight-member, and curved-member shear must meet paragraphs 5-2 (properly 5-3 for section location), 5-4, and 5-5 respectively.
sections.body: [p. 38] a. The shear strength Vc provided by concrete must be computed according to ACI 318-19 except in the cases described in this chapter. b. Shear strength of cantilever walls must meet the requirements of paragraph 5-2. c. Shear strength of special straight members must meet the requirements of paragraph 5-4. d. Shear strength of curved members must meet the requirements of paragraph 5-5.
key_points: Vc must be computed according to ACI 318-19 except as described in this chapter; cantilever walls, special straight members and curved members must meet paragraphs 5-2, 5-4 and 5-5 (p. 38)
